column1: # manifests/bootloader-blobs.tsv — the COMMITTED source of truth for every byte
# lib/write-bootloader.sh is allowed to write into the 16 MB raw bootloader gap.
# The writer reads this file and nothing else to answer three questions:
#   1. WHICH blobs does this board×variant tuple write?  (the rows for the tuple,
#      in the order they appear here — that IS the dd order)
#   2. WHERE does each one go?  (write-bootloader.sh's blob-name → sector table;
#      deliberately NOT a column here, because an offset is on-disk geometry
#      frozen by docs/partition-contract.md, not per-package data)
#   3. IS THIS THE RIGHT BLOB?  (the sha256 column, asserted before the dd and
#      re-asserted against a READBACK of the image after it)
# A tuple with no rows here is REFUSED. That is the point: the writer cannot be
# handed a blob it has never been told about, so a silently-wrong .deb — an
# archive re-spin under an unchanged version, a stale staged package, the OTHER
# board's payload — fails the build against a committed pin instead of producing
# a plausible image that bricks a board.
# COLUMNS (tab-separated)
#   board     board_id (manifest board_id, the value passed as --board)
#   variant   family variant name, or `default` for the production vendor path
#   package   Debian package the blob ships in (pinned in armbian-bsp-deb-versions.txt)
#   version   that package's exact pinned Debian version
#   blob      blob filename inside the package payload
#   sha256    lowercase hex SHA-256 of that blob's bytes
# PROVENANCE, and it is re-derivable from this file alone. Every hash below was
# read out of a .deb whose own SHA-256 matched that package's entry in the
# bookworm/main/arm64 `Packages` index at https://apt.armbian.com — the digest
# taken from the gpgv-VERIFIED `Release` plaintext, never the raw `InRelease` —
# under both pinned archive keys DF00FAF1C577104B50BF1D0093D6889F9F0E78D5 and
# 8CFA83D13EB2181EEF5843E41EB30FAF236099FE. The `package` + `version` columns are
# the pins in manifests/armbian-bsp-deb-versions.txt, and the verification is the
# pipeline's own lib/fetch-debs-auth.sh (auth_keyring_has_exact_fingerprints ->
# auth_verify_release_to_file -> auth_release_has_identity), i.e. the exact code
# a real BSP fetch runs — so a fresh checkout can reproduce every row without any
# local artifact. Do NOT cite a path under test-results/ here: that tree is
# gitignored repo-local evidence (Rule D) and resolves to nothing when cloned.
# TWO PAYLOAD SHAPES, and only one of them is a split. The `-current`/`-edge`
# packages on BOTH boards, and the Rock's `-vendor` package, ship ONE unified
# `u-boot-rockchip.bin` carrying idbloader (RKNS at blob offset 0) and the U-Boot
# FIT (d00dfeed at 0x7f8000) together — a single dd at sector 64 lays both, and
# the blob must NEVER be split. Only `linux-u-boot-orangepi5-plus-vendor` (the
# 2017.09 Rockchip fork) ships the historical `idbloader.img` + `u-boot.itb`
# pair, which is why that ONE tuple has two rows. Do not add split handling for
# any other tuple — no other pinned package contains those files.
# `edge-test` and `vendor-patched` intentionally carry the VENDOR U-Boot rows:
# neither board declares a `variant_overrides.<that variant>.uboot_packages`, so
# the resolver hands them the board's top-level (vendor) package and these rows
# record what will actually be written. They are not aspirational.
# board
# PRODUCTION (vendor): U-Boot 2017.09 Rockchip fork, closed rkbin BL31.
orangepi5-plus
orangepi5-plus
# EDGE: U-Boot 2026.01, TF-A compiled from ARM-software v2.13.0 (mainline).

# shape as its -current/-edge siblings; the bytes still differ, hence its own row.
